steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We're only a few hours away from the sunrise Miss Ines stipulated.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We need to hurry up the pace of our evacuation op.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Say, haven't you forgotten something even more important, Doctor of Rhodes Island?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Yes, we and Dublinn are starting from the same line again.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Which means, time is of the essence.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: To forever abide by commitments is not solely what we ask of ourselves... but of those we make deals with, too.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: You've finally made it. I almost got offed by that Redsteel Guard boy.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Her Grace is very dissatisfied with your indolence. Your methods are too tepid.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Or is it that you're coaxing Alexandrina? Playing on her sympathies?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: That's a very grave accusation. I'm unconditionally loyal to Her Grace, that much is obvious, I'm just...

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: We'll review your excuses in hindsight. For now, though, there's no time.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Stay put, Rhodes Islanders.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What are you doing?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Arts in black... Just as the fresh intel described.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: You've kept it very well hidden, Rhodes Island. To think this Cautus is the Sarkaz's very Lord of Fiends.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Very interesting... Perhaps this is an issue that can't be solved without you.

spans.text: an issue that can't be solved without you.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Poet, to not have recognized this is a further failure of your duties.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: By what means does Her Grace hope for me to remedy this?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: While you were chatting with Dublinn, we've had the position of the airship's dock confirmed. It's... treacherous in there.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: But our fresh intel tells us the 'Lord of Fiends' will have some way to handle it.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: So, little Lord of Fiends, you'll cooperate with us, won't you.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: And what about that Windermere girl?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Forget trying to make up for things. The technology of the airship is our number one priority.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Think we've notified about everyone we could find.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: And that... caps off all we can do.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Amiya isn't back yet, and neither the Doctor nor Ines have been in touch.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Looks like somewhere's caught fire outside again.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: That's—where the hotel is.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: We'd better go take a look.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: *pant*... *pant*...

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Delphine? What are you sprinting like that for?

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: —Where's that Rhodes Island lot?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I'll lay this out straight. Listen up, Alexandrina Vina Victoria.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Amiya and the Doctor got pushed by the 'Trilby Asher' into fulfilling that deal. They need to find the airship.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Duke Wellington's army is on this plate already. Afraid Duke Caster's reinforcements are here too.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: They're all out to win the technology behind that Sarkaz airship. None of them will let their rivals have the advantage of getting it first.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Norport's become the dukes' wrestling ring.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Hah. Surprising exactly no one.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: What about that broadcast? You know, pushing the dukes into officially attacking this place—

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Miss Ines says she'll do all she can to make it happen.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: To what? What are you telling us?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: She says, she needs until sunrise.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Got it.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Assuming the dukes go with direct confrontation after all, how much time do we still have?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: As long as Miss Ines succeeds... the Duke of Windermere's high-speed warship should be approaching not long after the sun comes up.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You've got a hell of a lot of people gathered here.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: The people who aren't here probably already got the news. Anyone who does want to come with us'll keep with the procession.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: So I suggest before the Duke's warship officially encroaches, we continue to wait here.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: With the present circumstances... going out in the street's not a good idea.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Doesn't matter if it's Wellington or Caster, they won't hold back against anyone they think's in the way.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: No. We're best off leaving now.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The Sarkaz barracks around the barricade wall got ambushed. Odds are more than likely some duke's forces did it.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We should get as close as we can to the part of the wall that's thin on defenses, while it's still night.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: More importantly... we need to let them all know, everyone still peeping out from behind their windows, that what we said was true.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: This evacuation isn't some scheme to nab the last of their reserves. It's not some Sarkaz trap to wipe them out.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Reestablishing trust is a challenge, and the one and only way to do it—

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Is for them to see real action.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: Here, the books you asked me for last time.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: I had to spend an age searching in those Londinium libraries, not even knowing Victorian. Grabbed some poor Feline in the end to find your stuff.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: Sometimes I see you writing and drawing in this blank book too.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: You don't just read, you write your own stuff too?

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: I've never been to Kazdel, but I hear they've got a whole Sarkaz university underground there.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: Are you a teacher there?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: No, I'm just like you. Putting my life up for sale.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: Are these books really that fun to read?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: They all end fine enough, but similar events keep happening over and over.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: All the authors can do is keep writing fine enough endings.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: And I've gotten sick of it.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: General Manfred made us lock you in here, but hasn't given any further orders since...

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: How did you offend him?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Maybe, he just thought jail would be more peaceful for me.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: It's easier in here... to do whatever I'd actually like to do.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: And that's reading?

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: You really are a boring guy, then.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: I hear... us Sarkaz are going to get some real good news, real soon.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: So good it'll stun the entire land!

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: It's just going to be another war.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: Has anyone ever told you you're a drag to talk to?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Honestly, yeah.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: Seriously... what a drag.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: Alright, I'm changing shifts. You behave in here.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: Don't forget, you promised to pay me for the books—
The Royal Court soldier's silhouette disappears with a wobble into the end of the prison corridor, and very soon, a different set of footsteps comes into earshot.
Hoederer waits.
But there is only quiet.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: The crew are all aboard the airship now.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Understood.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Paprika.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Urk... Here!

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Have you ever read a book called... A History of Sarkaz War?

spans.text: Have you ever read a book called...

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You should. I have a copy in my drawer. You can take it.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Is it a very fancy story?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: It is a history annals.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: You said that already...

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Then you shouldn't be asking that sort of question.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I disapprove of near to every viewpoint expressed in it. The weakness, the grief, the crushing.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: But still, I recognize that it is a book whose pages are soaked in blood.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: How would the writer describe the war we're seeing right now?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I'm as curious as you.
